title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
summary: Determine the highest frequency an element can achieve in an array by performing at most k increment operations on any element.
statement: Determine the highest frequency an element can achieve in an array by performing at most k increment operations on any element.
constraints: At most k operations may each increment one element by one; decrements are forbidden.
Return the largest achievable frequency of a single value.
reference_solution:
def maximum_frequency_after_increments(nums, k):
 nums=sorted(nums);left=0;total=0;answer=1
 for right,value in enumerate(nums):
  total+=value
  while value*(right-left+1)-total>k:total-=nums[left];left+=1
  answer=max(answer,right-left+1)
 return answer

hints: After sorting, an optimal group is a contiguous window raised to its rightmost value.
Maintain the window sum so its raising cost is target*length-sum.
Move left while cost exceeds k and track the largest valid window.
Any skipped value between chosen sorted values costs no more than a chosen smaller value, so an optimal selection is contiguous and the sliding window considers it.
